Despite the order dated 03.09.2019 by which notices were issued on the opposite party no. 2 and according to the report dated 25.10.2019, the opposite party no. 2 received the notice personally,
there is no representation on her part.
The original copy of the second supplementary affidavit is being put on record.

The present petition has been preferred for the quashing of the order dated 28.05.2019 passed by the learned Patna High Court CR. MISC. dt.23-03-2023 refusal, then she was physically assaulted by them and even her 'stridhan' was taken away and subsequently she was also assaulted by the husband.
Accordingly, the case.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submit that the petitioners are sister-in-law (nanad) and brother-in-law (nandoshi).

Further, due to stay in the present case pursuant to the order dated 03.09.2019, the proceeding so far as the petitioner no. 1, namely, Sujata Kumari @ Guriya Devi, and petitioner no. 2, namely, Krishna Murari Prasad @ Krishna Murari are concerned, the same could not be taken up.
However, so far as the husband and other family members are concerned, the proceeding continued.

Further, in the meantime good sense prevailed upon the parties and the couple came to an amicable settlement followed by joint submission of compromise petition on 23.10.2019 and it would be proper to bring the same on record.

sentences.text: That the present case and the Matrimonial case is pending since long and nothing tangibale decision has arrived.
4. That the parties are unnecessary being harassed in appearing in both the cases and huge money is being spent.
5. That due to certain misunderstanding between both the parties the informant has instituted this case and now entire grievance of both the parties have been settled.
6. That after this the informant does not wants to proceed with the case further.
7. That there is no public policy involved in this case.
8. That the aforesaid settlement has arrived at in between the parties on this own sweet will and without any coercion and pressure from any quarter.

9. That in the present case both the parties have agreed that they will not take any steps further in any other case which might they have filed pending in any court either of civil nature of criminal nature and take steps to get the same dismissed each other in future.

10. That the parties have further agreed that after this case/cases non of the parties in Patna High Court CR. MISC. No. 44932 of 2019(6) dt.23-03-2023 future will file against each other and if filed the same become redundant and will not stand in any court of law.
11. That in token of settlement arrived at both the parties as well as their respective lawyers have put their signed on this petition."

Subsequently, the matter was taken up by the Court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate,
Patna in G.R. Case No. 9050/18 and taking into account the compromise petition vide its order dated 25.10.2015, the learned Court was pleased to acquit the other co-accused being the husband (Dr. Vivek Ranjan), the mother-in-law (Gita Sinha), the father-in-law (Bipin Kumar Sinha) as well as one of his brother.

As stated above, there is no representation from the opposite party no. 2 despite valid service of notice.

In the aforementioned circumstances, taking into account the compromise petition that has come on record by way of supplementary affidavit as also the order dated 25.10.2015 by which the other accused persons were acquitted which has been brought by way of second supplementary affidavit,
this Court has no option but to allow the present petition.

The order dated 28.05.2019 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Patna in connection with G.R. Case No. 9050 of 2018 arising out of Hawai Adda P.S. Case No. 271 of 2018 under sections 498A, 504 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act stands quashed.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Further, in the meantime good sense prevailed upon the parties and the couple came to an amicable settlement followed by joint submission of compromise petition on 23.10.2019 and it would be proper to bring the same on record.
"1. That due to intervention of well wisher and common friends both the parties have agreed and decided to file and application U/S 13(B) of Hindu Marriage Act for Mutual Divorce the present Matrimonial (Divorce) case bearing Matrimonial Case No. 1171 of 2018 pending disposal before principal Judge, Family Court at Patna initiated by Dr. Vivek Ranjan for Divorce out Patna High Court CR.
2. That after this the case cordial relation has been restored between the parties.
9. That in the present case both the parties have agreed that they will not take any steps further in any other case which might they have filed pending in any court either of civil nature of criminal nature and take steps to get the same dismissed each other in future.
10. That the parties have further agreed that after this case/cases non of the parties in Patna High Court CR. MISC. No. 44932 of 2019(6) dt.23-03-2023 future will file against each other and if filed the same become redundant and will not stand in any court of law.
In the aforementioned circumstances, taking into account the compromise petition that has come on record by way of supplementary affidavit as also the order dated 25.10.2015 by which the other accused persons were acquitted which has been brought by way of second supplementary affidavit,
this Court has no option but to allow the present petition.
The petition preferred under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is allowed.
